chapter_title: Concerning the Seed Grain that shall be formed by
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

** ¶2:** These interior truths — both celest ial and natural — that are perceived within the mind shall be formed and adorned by the five fundamental fac ulties of the spiritual person . Now , both the ardor of love and the severity of its apparent withdrawal serve to nourish interior truth and the whole perception that grows from it. For just as these contrary states together sustain the growth of perception, so also perception is laid waste when the influx of good and truth is altogether wit hheld — that is, through spiritual deprivation.

**¶ 3:** In this same manner , Divine Order draws all five fac ulties of the spirit into unity within itself.

**¶4:** In this same manner also , a def iciency and a failing of good and truth shall pass from one spiritual state to another through these faculties; and those who have freely received Divine Good have gathered interior truths into themselves, adorned their understanding with them, and made them their own — while spiritual temptation shall arise for them through the very faculties that remain disordered.

**¶ 5:** Those within the church shall also be caused to fall into falsity on account of these faculties, through the active force of the self hood that dwells in them. The prop rium has cast its obsc urity over them, just as it shall also cast its obscurity over the spiritual fac ulties themselves and corrupt the goods of life produced by every form of perception and knowledge.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: "In this way also Righteousness gathers the five to it.

"In this way too, a lack and a shortfall shall occur from place to place through them; and they who have chosen it have gathered it in and beautified and attained it, while an affliction shall arise for it through those.

"People also shall be caused to stumble on their account, through the energy of Matter that dwells in them. It has poured its shadow over them, just as it shall also pour its shadow over the elements and destroy the fruits of all the trees."

"This seed grain and this barley grain that you see shall be formed and [adorned] and beautified by the five elements. Now, the warmth and the cold nourish the seed grain and the entire tree. So, just as these things nourish it [and cause it to grow, so also] it is destroyed [and laid waste] through [great] hunger.

fills.fill: and cause it to grow, so also
